title: Draft: CGMDETM-151379: Central runtime DB disconnect recovery
description:
Closes CGMDETM-151379.

## Goal

Recover a runtime FastObjects disconnect centrally in TMWinDB. New DB work waits while one recovery cycle runs. Replayable reads resume against reopened native handles. Operations with uncertain side effects fail closed through the existing restart path instead of being replayed. No operation-specific retry logic is added to callers.

## Recovery contract

- `RecoveryOperationGate` is the admission point for TMWinDB operations. Its states are Open, Freezing, Recovering, Failed, and ShuttingDown.
- Top-level work is uncertain by default. Stable reads opt into replay only where the complete operation can be repeated safely.
- Writes, transactions, locks, iterators, OQL bindings, streams, and other lifetime-bound native work retain an uncertain lease until completion.
- A recoverable read failure freezes admission, releases the triggering read root, drains already admitted replayable work, and lets exactly one owner run recovery.
- Any active uncertain root, drain timeout, reopen failure, or healing failure latches restart-required state. Waiting callers are never released onto a partially recovered database.
- Native wrappers carry a recovery generation. Old handles are rejected after publish, and handles created by the recovery thread become valid only when that generation is published.

## Auto-healing

Recovery uses global barriers across every registered database:

1. Disconnect every base. Any ambiguous disconnect fails the attempt closed.
2. Connect and open every base.
3. Heal every database before publishing success.

The healing phase rebuilds the persistent root lock, dictionary and class metadata caches, `GlobalObjectId` bindings, loaded `DBRef` object caches, object watches, notification queues, cached `DBList` AllSets, and their watches. The live-list registry is synchronized so filtered-list destruction cannot race recovery or notification dispatch.

## Boundaries

- `RecoveryOperation.h` is a scalar-only public lease API. Native synchronization remains in `RecoveryOperationGate.h`, keeping the public `DBRef` include graph compatible with `/clr`.
- The application layer only installs recovery and restart hooks, then explicitly enables runtime recovery after database startup. Recovery policy, blocking, replay, generation checks, and cache healing remain in TMWinDB.
- `RecoveryBoundaryArchitectureTest` prevents ordinary runtime modules from introducing direct FastObjects includes or operation-level recovery control. Existing explicit FastObjects boundary owners are TMWinDB, TMAdmin, TMPtSecurity, TMDict, TMTestSuite, and package code.

## Validation on MR head `5de5c5302cd`

- `TMWinDB` Debug Win32: full source compile and DLL link passed.
- `TMTestSuite` Debug Win32: full source compile and executable link passed.
- `TMCommonObjects` Debug Win32 `/clr`: full source compile and managed DLL link passed.
- Recovery-focused suite: 71 tests from 10 suites passed.
- Real FastObjects integration: actual `TMObjectDB`, `DBWriteRef`, `DBRef`, and `DBList` tests passed in LOCAL mode.
- Self-triggered outage: `LazyDBRefTriggersRecoveryAfterTransportDrop` passed 10 of 10 repeated runs with stop-on-first-failure enabled.
- TurboMed was not started for these checks.

The focused suite covers gate admission and drain behavior, uncertainty escalation, shutdown, generation publication and invalidation, strict disconnect/connect/open/heal barriers, cache failure handling, runtime restart behavior, disconnect error classification, dictionary healing, architecture ownership, and six production-shaped DB reference/list scenarios.

## Mutation proof

During implementation, each of these deliberate defects made a focused test fail:

- omit native `open()` during recovery
- omit cache healing
- omit generation publication
- omit `GlobalObjectId` rebinding
- omit the closed-base recovery trigger

Each mutation was reverted before the final build.

## Local dependency note

The workstation cache does not contain the exact ignored package revisions currently requested by `develop` for Stingray, Kocops, and TBarCode. The merged source was built with adjacent cached package headers and provisioned dependency import libraries. TMWinDB, TMTestSuite, and TMCommonObjects outputs themselves were rebuilt from this MR head. CI remains the exact-package validation gate.

## Review map

- Admission, uncertainty, shutdown, generation: `RecoveryOperation.*`, `RecoveryOperationGate.h`
- Runtime ownership and publication: `ptdisconnecthandler.*`, `TMPoet.*`
- Three-phase reopen and cache healing: `RuntimeReopen.h`, `TMObjectDB.*`
- Reference replay and rebinding: `StorableRefImp.cpp`, `GlobalObjectId.cpp`
- Lifetime-bound uncertain work: transaction, lock, iterator, OQL, stream, and user-manager wrappers
- Proof: `DisconnectEnforcement/*Recovery*`, `RuntimeReopenTest.cpp`, and `IntegrationTests/TMObjectDBTestFixture.*`
